narrowResearchQuestion: For a frozen CooperScene release, quantify whether the distributed four-ego index, the paper's three-vehicle-ego protocol, and indexes regenerated by the fixed public converter are equivalent for artifact content, evaluation population, paired method comparisons, and equal-event-exposure training.
defensibleNoveltyBoundary: The potentially novel unit is the complete package: release-versus-regeneration manifest parity, explicit vehicle and infrastructure cohorts, physical-event paired method inference, and equal-event-exposure training ablation. Ego selection, vehicle-versus-infrastructure tasks, or clustered resampling alone are established components.

releasedArchive.finding: CRC-verified mini indexes contain four ego projections per physical event and label the dataset OPV2V.

publicConverterHistory.finding: Every public converter version permits only vehicle ego IDs 1, 2, and 3 and writes dataset=CooperScene. The public history does not expose the generator of the earlier four-ego release indexes.

paperProtocol.finding: Section 4 describes iterating over the three vehicles as ego, using infrastructure as a cooperator, and averaging over ego vehicles.

frozenCohorts.definition: Distributed release indexes with four ego projections per physical event.
Vehicle-ego rows 1, 2, and 3 selected from the distributed release indexes.
Indexes regenerated by the fixed public converter at a recorded commit and environment.
Infrastructure-ego row 0 selected from the distributed release indexes and reported as a separate task.

primaryEstimands: Vehicle-only pooled AP and physical-event macro-averaged vehicle AP under RV3.
Infrastructure-only AP under RI, never folded into a vehicle-ego population without an explicit target mixture.
Same-model paired difference between RV3 and G3 at matched physical event and vehicle ego.
Difference-in-differences for whether a protocol choice changes the comparison between two frozen methods.
Full AP recomputed inside a paired physical-event bootstrap; moving-block or take-level leave-one-out sensitivity when events are serially or session dependent.
forbiddenShortcuts: Do not derive an effective-sample-size correction and apply it mechanically to AP.
Do not call receiver-conditioned projections duplicate acquisitions or assume independence between them.
Do not claim metric inflation, ranking reversal, or benchmark invalidity before paired outcomes are computed.
Do not merge infrastructure ego with vehicle ego merely because both appear in one release index.
Do not attribute a published table to one index contract without command, commit, checkpoint, and artifact provenance.
evaluationPlan: Freeze canonical manifests for R4, RV3, G3, and RI, including event, ego, source paths, annotations, metainfo, and converter environment.
Run at least two frozen official checkpoints or reproducibly trained baselines and cache prediction and ground-truth inputs needed to recompute full AP.
Join every outcome to the frozen physical-event and ego key because the public evaluator retains only sample_idx and pools global AP.
Report RV3, RI, R4, and G3 separately before any target-mixture analysis.
Use event-paired intervals for method differences and predeclare moving-block and take-level sensitivity analyses.

arms: Random1: one randomly selected vehicle ego per event and epoch.
Cyclic1: one deterministically cycled vehicle ego per event and epoch.
All3: all three vehicle ego projections, with event-averaged loss.
Same-ego-triple: repeated identical ego projection as a positive control for row-count-only augmentation.
trainingAblation.primaryControl: Match unique physical-event slots and optimizer steps across arms. Report a separate compute-matched analysis rather than conflating compute and event exposure.
trainingAblation.inference: Use paired seeds and event-level outcomes; treat the same-ego-triple arm as a diagnostic, not a realistic training strategy.

nearestWorkBoundary.boundary: Ego selection in cooperative datasets is established and is not itself the contribution.
Vehicle-centric and infrastructure-centric cooperative tasks are already separated; an infrastructure-ego cohort alone is not novel.

nearestWorkBoundary.work: Approximate Randomization for Comparing Machine Translation Systems
nearestWorkBoundary.boundary: Paired resampling for method comparison is established methodology.
Bootstrap stability of challenge rankings is established.
Hierarchical resampling is established; the novelty must come from the artifact-specific parity and controlled protocol package.

positiveResult: A preregistered material difference appears in release parity, a paired method comparison, or an equal-event-exposure training conclusion and survives the full cohort and dependence sensitivity analysis.
negativeResult: Every primary comparison lies inside a preregistered equivalence margin, producing a useful machine-checkable protocol-equivalence certificate for the frozen release and converter.
killCriteria: The full release cannot be mapped to stable physical-event and ego keys.
No fixed checkpoint, reproducible baseline, or sufficient cached prediction can support full paired AP recomputation.
RV3 and G3 cannot be aligned at identical physical events and vehicle egos.
A primary work already publishes the same four-part package for CooperScene.
The result survives only row-wise resampling and disappears under every event-aware analysis.
panelEntryRequirements: Complete full-release R4, RV3, G3, and RI manifest parity.
Run at least one frozen model end to end and cache per-projection outputs.
Demonstrate one paired event-level AP result with the preregistered cohort decomposition.
Confirm that the full package, rather than a generic resampling or subgroup-reporting component, remains the claimed contribution.
